basics.name: Han YANG
basics.label: B.Sc. in Animal Science | Aspiring Researcher in Computational Religion & Digital Humanities
basics.summary: An interdisciplinary researcher bridging animal science, applied mathematics, and computational methods. Incoming M.A. student in Religious Studies (MARS) at The Chinese University of Hong Kong. Passionate about applying computational approaches — NLP, complex systems, and mathematical modeling — to the study of classical Chinese philosophy and traditional knowledge systems.

publications.name: Research on Multi-Object Localization of Rocket Debris
publications.publisher: Frontier and Progress of Computational Mathematics and Modeling
publications.summary: Developed a rocket debris recovery strategy using sonic booms by optimizing WGS84-based tri-sphere and quad-sphere intersection models. Employed MATLAB, including lsqnonlin and a novel traversal algorithm, to implement a weighted least squares correction model validated by Monte Carlo simulations.

projects.name: ESI — Curvature Modeling of Egg Trajectories: Morphological Effects
projects.summary: Led a team to invent and design an egg rolling test rig, collecting 90 egg samples. Innovatively converted 3D motion into 2D planar motion. Utilized MATLAB with Kalman filtering to extract dynamic behavioral features from video sequences. Applied polynomial fitting to analyze the impact of egg shape index and eccentricity on trajectory.
highlights: One JCR Q1 research paper planned for publication

projects.name: Machine Vision for Coupled Egg Dynamics & Intelligent Sorting
projects.summary: Led literature review on coupling mechanism of egg morphology, contact interface characteristics, dynamic rolling behavior, and intelligent sorting prediction. Systematically summarized 240 recent review articles and drafted an initial review manuscript.
highlights: One JCR Q1 review paper planned for publication

projects.name: Mathematical Modeling Competitions (Team Leader)
projects.summary: Led a team in paper writing, modeling, and programming for multiple mathematical modeling competitions. Notable work includes finite element skull modeling using Ogden constitutive model, and polar angle iteration with Simpson's numerical integration for dragon formation coiling simulation.
highlights: Over 50 competition awards across dozens of contests
